strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates limitations of task-specific models and existing multitask approaches without heterogeneity awareness
Principled technical design: geometric mean reference ensures modulation factors maintain mean 1; two-level modulation (sample and task) addresses heterogeneity systematically
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 10 diverse behavioral tasks, multiple RL baselines (GRPO/RLOO/GPG/RE++), systematic ablations, qualitative reasoning analysis
Strong empirical results: best average rank (1.20), substantial improvements on weak tasks (SAR +17%, HUM +42%), consistent across methods
Reproducibility and transparency: detailed hyperparameters, complete reward design specifications, algorithm pseudocode, promise of code release
Insightful empirical analysis: Figure 4 directly links advantage modulation to weak-task learning, advantage distributions justify approach, modulation factor dynamics examined
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution is GRPO with geometric-mean advantage modulation; advantage reweighting and multitask balancing are well-established (Kendall et al. 2018, Yu et al. 2020)
Single-domain evaluation: experiments only on Human Behavior Atlas benchmark; unclear if HARPO generalizes to other multitask RL domains (robotics, vision, non-social NLP)

Experimental concerns: LLM-judge evaluation for 3/10 tasks introduces brittleness; some baselines show suspiciously poor performance (GRPO HUM: 27.56%, RE++ INT: 5.01%) suggesting implementation/tuning issues; no confidence intervals or multiple runs
Hyperparameter choices lack justification: βρ=0.95, βs=0.95 appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis; missing comparison to simpler baselines (uniform weighting, inverse variance)
Generalization validation incomplete: held-out evaluation on only 2 tasks within same domain; modest improvement on AUT (+2%); no out-of-domain generalization demonstrated

Reward design not thoroughly ablated: multiple components (task accuracy, format, length) combined with fixed weights; no ablation on these design choices or sensitivity analysis; weights appear domain-specific
Modest ablation effect sizes: sample-level modulation rank change 2.60→1.90 is small; structured modulation 2.00→1.90 very small; raises questions about component necessity
Reasoning quality analysis primarily qualitative: Figures 2-3 show few cherry-picked examples; reasoning length statistics only in Figure 1; no automated metrics for reasoning quality
Missing related work comparisons: no evaluation against other multitask optimization methods (gradient surgery, task normalization, uncertainty weighting for reasoning RL)
No computational overhead analysis: training time or memory costs compared to GRPO not reported
